best_for: Developers and analysts who write SQL against several database engines every day and want one IDE with schema-aware completion, free for hobby use and paid at work.

points.title: Free for non-commercial use
points.text: Individuals can use DataGrip free for non-commercial work such as learning and hobby projects. If you are paid for the work, even by a non-profit, you need a commercial subscription. Companies cannot use the free license. A 30-day trial is available.

points.title: The free license has strings
points.text: It needs a JetBrains Account and online activation, with no offline codes. Anonymous usage statistics are always sent, with no opt-out. The license lasts a year and renews only if you used it in the last six months.

points.title: Many databases, one window
points.text: It connects to more than 50 databases, among them PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle, SQLite, Snowflake, BigQuery, ClickHouse, MongoDB and Redis, and can find cloud instances on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure.

points.title: SQL help that knows your schema
points.text: Completion, error checks and quick-fixes use the real tables and columns of the connected database, across dialects. Results open in tables you can filter, sort and edit, then export.

points.title: AI agents work under your rules
points.text: You can plug in agents such as Junie, Claude, Codex, GitHub Copilot or Gemini CLI. They get schema context, but run under permissions and confirmations, with an optional read-only mode, and their queries land in history.

points.title: Needs a recent machine
points.text: JetBrains asks for 8 GB of RAM, 10 GB of disk and a 4-core CPU, on Windows 10 or 11, macOS 26 or 27, or a recent Linux. Java is bundled, so no separate install.

points.title: Where the builds come from
points.text: Windows installers are x64 and Arm64, per user or all users, and the Windows listing keeps 80 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source, such as the Toolbox App, which can roll back. The Linux Flatpak is not verified on Flathub.
